exposure: Immediate postpartum copper intrauterine device (IUD) insertion
cohort: Women who received immediate postpartum IUD insertion at vaginal delivery or cesarean section between March 2018 and December 2019 at a Brazilian public university hospital
finding: Despite a higher expulsion rate associated with immediate postpartum IUD insertion, the rate of long-term continuation of intrauterine contraception was high.
mod_finding: The IUD expulsion rate was higher after vaginal delivery compared to cesarean section (68.4% vs 31.6%, p = 0.031).
